target_customer: African fintechs and software companies issuing cards (original); African consumers and merchants using ChitChat (current)
problem: Card issuing in Africa required a bank or third party processor and was slow; consumers face high cross-border payment fees.
business_model: Card issuing API earning interchange and processing fees; later a messaging and payments super app
product_category: Card issuing API, now messaging and payments wallet

founders.name: Perseus Mlambo
previous_startups: Zazu (challenger bank in Zambia, raised over 2M dollars)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch October 2021: Union54 spun out of Zazu, launched about six years earlier.

founders.name: Alessandra Martini
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch describes Mlambo and Martini as a couple who co-founded Zazu and Union54.

technical_complexity.rationale: Card issuing with BIN sponsorship, processing and settlement across several countries needed scheme relationships and fraud controls; by October 2021 four companies were live.

defensibility.rationale: Mastercard access via a partner and licensed issuer relationships were hard to copy, but the July 2022 chargeback fraud showed the risk of the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The founder claimed in 2021 it was the only African company giving fintechs interchange revenue. No source shows an incumbent copying or buying it.

market_need_then: African fintechs needed local card issuing; over 50 companies were in the API sandbox by October 2021 per TechCrunch.

branding.name_origin: Inspired by Africa's 54 countries, per TechCrunch coverage seen in search results.

identity.voice_and_tone: Site tagline 'Modern card issuing, your brand first'; ChitChat described as a WeChat for Africa

branding.brand_signature: ChitChat as the consumer brand, called a WeChat for Africa
branding.community_and_virality: ChitChat launched with Mastercard in March 2024 with press from TechCabal and others.

brand_strength.rationale: Pan African name that fit the card API; press covered both the Y Combinator first for Zambia and the ChitChat launch, but a 2025 origins dispute and the 2022 fraud suspension hurt trust.

pivots.from: Card issuing API for African fintechs
pivots.to: ChitChat, an integrated messaging and payments wallet for consumers
pivots.why: After the July 2022 chargeback fraud and card suspension of about eleven months, the company relaunched as a consumer super app (TechCabal)

outcome_analysis: Union54 raised 3M dollars in October 2021 and 12M in April 2022, both led by Tiger Global, but in July 2022 it suspended card operations after a chargeback fraud attempt reported at 1.2 billion dollars and the halt lasted about eleven months. It relaunched in 2023 as ChitChat, launching with Mastercard in Zambia in March 2024. In September 2025 a lawsuit by Patrick Sikalinda claimed co-founder status and 33 percent equity, which the company denies. The pivot is not yet proven, so it is recorded as an unresolved risk.
notes: Competitors: TechCrunch October 2021 names no rivals, only partners; 2021 dated cross-border payments sources were not found, so the list is empty rather than listing undated 2025 pages. Total raised is about 15M dollars per Startup List Africa. Sikalinda's claim that he co-founded the company is disputed and he is not recorded as a founder; the YC page lists Mlambo and Martini. Founding year is 2021 per the YC page and TechCrunch; CB Insights says 2019. Status is Active on the YC page; the 2025 dispute is described by WeeTracker as unresolved.
